## Authority reuse and genuine gap

PTC already distinguishes its fitted subspace, exact application map and
frozen-component subtraction. Reuse that mathematics. MAP/JINC already own
their estimands and handoffs; a normalized product supplies no automatic sky
model. NOI already distinguishes conditional transformation uncertainty from
relearning and successor generations. The author should not rebuild those
contracts or the accepted empirical-governance framework.

The new scientific work is the conditional relation between target, selected
model, projection, removal, bypass, restoration and resulting response; how
learning changes that response; the causal sufficiency needed for restart;
and the meaning of completion, convergence and selected terminal products.
The approved limiting-case topics should expose the consequences of those
definitions. This is not a request for another explanation of UID 4460.

## Conflicts and unresolved choices

- The September 1 sequence and older author-input list required numerical
  qualification before the prior form of authorship. The September 6 decision
  explicitly permits this conditional core only. Old approved bytes remain
  unchanged; they do not block this preparation or admit a numerical method.
- Historical checkpoint descriptions cannot prove all future causal state is
  complete. Only the scientific identity convention is extracted; causal
  completeness follows the newly approved scope.
- Frozen MAP and JINC documents include historical candidate-status text.
  Their exact freeze records govern scientific status. Freeze does not supply
  missing coefficients, numerical adequacy or unavailable companion products.
- NOI-ODQ-110C is an approved boundary, not a whole-package freeze.
- The model, projector, recurrence, learning, stopping and uncertainty choices
  remain unselected. The manager identifies no further core-level choice
  needed before attempting the conditional derivation. If a derivation proves
  otherwise, its exact missing premise must return to the owner.
